narrativeProgression.description: Lova introduces a framework for achieving a balanced life using the metaphor of a three-legged table.
Lova paints an ideal world where people pursue their passions.
He contrasts this with the reality where money often dictates choices.
He introduces the concept of "filling holes" with overconsumption when feeling unfulfilled.
Lova proposes a simple idea to address this: a framework for a balanced life.
He defines life based on three areas: health, wealth, and relationships.
He uses the metaphor of a three-legged table to explain the need for balance.
Lova shares an anecdote about a friend who overfocused on his business, neglecting other aspects of his life.
He stresses the interconnectedness of the three areas and the dangers of neglecting any one of them.
Lova emphasizes that understanding this idea and using tracking systems can lead to long-term success and freedom to pursue passions.

text_to_speech: Hey there as many of you know, only half of my speech got recorded at TEDx Rotterdam. So the second half is still the original but I tried to recreate the first half and i hope you enjoy it. The mic is over there. Imagine you could wake up to a world where you have the freedom to pursue your passions and become the best you can be what if i told you it's easier than you think and everyone can do it. But we live in a society where money rules our world and this can have a profound effect on your life so you might get out of college and get a job that pays the bills rather than go for a job that feeds your soul. You might go out into the world and grab a partner that seems nice but isn't the one for you. Because you're afraid of being lonely. In our society everything is available to you so you might seek out to fill your holes with an overconsumption of food, gadgets, and information and this makes you overstimulated. What if i tell you that with a simple little idea you can take the first step to design the life that you dream about and actually live it. About four to five years ago I discovered something by looking for the commonalities between all of my successful mentors, and what I discovered changed the way i thought the world worked. And most of all it changed the way I live and define my life. The way I define life is actually very simple there are three areas where you can put any and every problem into. Each area has an internal and external component. The areas are health, wealth, and relationships to give you an example take relationships. The external is the one we see like our friends and family, and the internal is the relationship we have with ourselves. Do we appreciate who we are, are we happy with what we've accomplished. What everyone seems to leave out is that everything is connected. Screw up one area in your life and everything will go down slowly but surely. Improve one area in your life and everything will start going up, slowly but surely. Let's take building a three-legged table for a second if you focus on building only one leg the table won't stand. If you overfocus on one leg the table will be slanted, so the key is to have a balanced focus while you're working on all three elements simultaneously. So the other day I was talking to a friend and in the last couple of months he was over focusing on building his fifth business and he invested too much time and money into an idea that failed. And as he was going through that horrible process he started neglecting the other areas in his life. His relationships and his health and his girlfriend of several years couldn't handle it anymore and she left him. As i was talking to him he became aware once again how the three areas are connected and that his health could suffer next, and that by focusing on improving all three areas again, starting with wealth, by building in accountability and several tracking systems it'll slowly but surely balance him out again and give him an opportunity to focus on his health and relationships. And it's this idea that most of the people I talk to seem to neglect. Everyone knows it exists but not everyone actively pursues a balance in their life which unfortunately results into many stories like my friend or maybe you might know someone who neglects his or her health or relationships, because he or she might live in a society that is made to get as much performance out of us as possible to put into our jobs, while neglecting the rest but as I just mentioned singling one area in your life can result in a long-term collapse while actively being aware and executing on the idea of having a balanced life with an optimal health, wealth, and relationships can result in a long-term success. I believe that this idea everyone should know that this idea and these trackers and systems exist. Because those are the key to unlocking freedom so that we can follow our passions and become the best we can be. That is why I believe this idea can make our lives a little bit better and that's why I believe this is an idea worth sharing.

youtube_description:
Work-life balance that is practical - TEDxRotterdam Side Event 1 September 2016. In this talk you will hear how to make work-life balance work for you in a practical way, without sacrificing anything. 

Join Me on the 100% FREE 30-DAY Work-Life Balance Challenge: http://www.whynot3.com/30-day-challenge/

Where I’ll show you the exact steps and specific directions to help you successfully create automation & tracking systems that will give you the ability to maintain your relationships, your business, and your health with minimal effort on your part – and you don’t need prior knowledge or a huge budget to do it…

Add me on Snapchat:    lovalink

Don't leave your work-life balance to be dictated by your business or your employer. Employers want to achieve the upmost productivity out of you, which is true. But it's up to you to tell them that even high intensity professional athletes take rest days, and that makes them more productive. Find this interesting system that is developed at why not 3 and shared on stage at TEDx Rotterdam

Family time, productivity, and personal time are all important factors if you want to have a balanced day, but yet these are only factors out of a big whole. We can divide life into health, wealth, and relationships and it's those that need to be focused on every day to really achieve that work-life balance and happiness that everyone craves.

You don't learn these things in school. It is realistic, and it is practical to achieve the idea of a work-life balance. It's a dream that everyone should pursue, as the activity will give you eudamonia, which is ultimate happiness like Aristotles said. The psychology behind it then is practicality.

In this TEDx Rotterdam talk you see the founder Lova Kremer talk about work-life balance as an entrepreneur. But most of all you see in this TEDx Rotterdam talk that he gives a model that he discovered by looking for the commonalities between all of his mentors. It's having a balance in that model that can potentially lead to long-term success.

Many TEDx Rotterdam talks focus on many great ideas, this is a potential idea worth spreading to say that a little bit of focus in each area can have great results overall. There is no need to completely forget other areas in your life, but also we can equally say that there is a need to be aware of all 3 areas. Because, if you're not aware of the work life balance principles, then you will not know what can happen to you over the long-term. 

Once you are aware you can start pursuing the ultimate eudamonia or happiness the way Aristotles described. In this Tedx Rotterdam talk we find out then that indeed there is something to be shared about work life balance, that is not fluffy but actually practical, and it's not ideallistic, because the people that have figured out life, and the real high-achievers are already implementing this.

Hope you enjoy this TEDx Rotterdam talk about work-life balance, and hopefully, it can inspire you to become better at what you do.

This TEDx Rotterdam talk was held during the side event I of 1 September 2016. 

If you're interested in talking about work-life balance principles that were discussed on TEDx Rotterdam, you're very welcome to contact us, and join our community. In this community we try and develop even more work-life balance lifehacks that people can use in their life with great success.

Work-life balance with peak productivity state in all areas of life is something that is not often discussed on the TEDx stage. However, work-life balance has gotten a bad rep in the last decades, as something that stops you from achieving ultimate productivity in your business. 
Nothing could be further from the truth. If you truly achieve a work-life balance you actually become more productive, and you will be able to handle more in your business. That's why it's so important to achieve the work-life balance that we talk about on the TEDx stage.

Remember simplicity is the key to solving your procrastination and achieving that balance that helps you focus properly and become more productive
